stories.headline: A toxic marble dump has become a tourist spot in Rajasthan
body: A 300-acre marble slurry dump near Kishangarh looks like snow and draws hundreds of tourists a day.
Nearby villagers say the dust ruins crops and causes coughs.
About 5,000 people live near the site.
stories.vc: Instagram tourism can't hide the health cost of industrial waste.

stories.headline: Badenoch says Britain should not apologise for the slave trade
body: Conservative leader Kemi Badenoch called an apology for Britain's slave-trade role a 'navel-gazing distraction'.
She said it would be used to push for financial reparations.
Andy Burnham said he is considering a formal apology before the Commonwealth summit.
stories.vc: Reparations debates shape Britain's ties with Commonwealth trade partners.

stories.headline: Arsenal win at Liverpool to go top of the Premier League
body: Arsenal beat Liverpool 1–0 at Anfield with a Kai Havertz goal.
It was their first win there in 14 attempts, since 2012.
They are now three points clear of Manchester City.
stories.joke: Thirteen years of trying. Turns out you just need Havertz.
stories.vc: Title races lift club revenue from broadcast and sponsors, and Arsenal's value with it.

stories.headline: CapGrid raises ₹50 crore to make precision parts
body: B2B manufacturing startup CapGrid raised ₹50 crore led by Hero Enterprise Venture Partners at a ₹430 crore valuation.
It will move into drone parts and data-centre components.
It made about ₹240 crore revenue in FY26 and expects ₹350 crore in FY27.
stories.joke: From car parts to drone parts. Upgrades all round.
stories.vc: 'Make in India' manufacturing platforms are drawing steady VC money as supply chains move away from China.

stories.headline: AU Small Finance Bank probes a possible data leak
body: AU Small Finance Bank is investigating a possible leak from a Salesforce-hosted platform with some vehicle-loan customer data.
Separately, a hacker allegedly listed admin access to Vijay Sales for $25,000.
AU says its own systems are unaffected; the Vijay Sales claim is unverified.
stories.vc: Third-party software is a growing weak spot, pushing Indian firms to spend more on vendor security.
